Dr. Partha Sarathi

In my experience of speaking to at least 6 surgeons before finalising to go ahead with Dr Partha, he was the most polite surgeon who looked at patients as curious humans, spent lot of time pre surgery to explain what will be done, answered all queries, did 24x7 telephone counselling and also was the one himself and not his team, to attend to my father after the surgery.

featured_reviews.name: Kiran Jhamb
featured_reviews.review_text:
I am from Chhattisgarh and suddenly developed severe imbalance to the extent that I was unable to stand properly. On the advice of our family neuro physician, we immediately consulted Dr. Arvind Kulkarni, a highly reputed neurosurgeon known to us through successful surgeries of our acquaintances.
After examining me and reviewing my MRI, Dr. Kulkarni advised immediate surgery. We chose Breach Candy Hospital because of its excellent reputation. The surgery was successfully performed on 28th March, and throughout the entire process, we received exceptional care and guidance.
The hospital facilities, especially the Super Deluxe Room arrangements, were outstanding. The nursing staff, paramedical team, and housekeeping staff were extremely caring, courteous, and professional.
Dr. Kulkarni’s counseling, clarity of explanation, patience in answering every query, and reassuring approach before and after surgery were remarkable. I would also especially like to thank Dr. Janardhan, a wonderful doctor and compassionate human being, who closely monitored my recovery and explained every detail with great care and positivity.
Today, I am able to stand on my feet again, and for that, my heartfelt gratitude goes to Dr. Kulkarni, Dr. Janardhan, and the entire team of Breach Candy Hospital. We shall always remain grateful for the excellent treatment and humane care provided to us.

I am Dr. Nurealam Siddiqui from Bangladesh. Recently, I was admitted to Jaslok Hospital and Research Center, Mumbai for urgent surgery for a pituitary adenoma under the care of the renowned and highly experienced neurosurgeon Dr. Raghvendra Ramadasi.

I found Jaslok Hospital and Research Center to be a highly specialized medical institution equipped with state-of-the-art facilities, providing excellent treatment with justified and transparent costs. featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst hospital experience and hospitality I have ever seen till now. If you come by bike, there is absolutely no parking facility for you. The hospital only provides parking and valet service for cars, which clearly shows they only care about people who own cars.

When I asked the watchman about bike parking, instead of helping properly, I was misguided and told that there is a nearby BMC parking available. That parking was almost 800 meters away from the hospital, and after going there, I found out that even the BMC parking does not allow bikes to be parked there. This practically means that if you come by bike, you are not welcome at this hospital. It feels like this hospital only gives preference to rich people who have cars, while others are ignored. If you don’t own a car, it is honestly better to visit a government hospital instead.

The second bad experience was with the hospital staff. When I asked about the OPD, the staff simply told me it was on the 3rd floor while I was already standing near the lift. After going upstairs, I realized that the OPD was actually located in another building. They should have clearly informed me that I needed to go to the other building instead of giving incomplete information. Because of this, I had to come back down and walk again to another building unnecessarily.

Zero humanity, zero hospitality, poor management, and no proper guidance for patients or visitors. Extremely disappointing experience.

Staying hydrated is just as important during the monsoon as it is in summer. Although the weather feels cooler, your body continues to lose fluids through daily activities. Proper hydration helps support normal body functions and overall well-being.

Here are a few simple tips to stay hydrated during the rainy season:

💧 Drink clean, safe drinking water regularly throughout the day.
🥥 Include fluids like coconut water, soups, or fresh fruit with high water content in your diet.
🍉 Eat seasonal fruits and vegetables after washing them thoroughly.
☕ Limit excessive caffeinated or sugary beverages, which may contribute to dehydration.
🧼 Carry a clean water bottle and maintain good hygiene to reduce the risk of waterborne illnesses.

Pay attention to signs such as excessive thirst, dark-colored urine, dizziness, or unusual fatigue, as these may indicate dehydration.

Maintaining healthy hydration habits, eating a balanced diet, and following good hygiene practices can help support your health during the monsoon season.

Monsoon season often brings an increase in fever-related illnesses, including dengue and viral fever. While both conditions may begin with a high temperature and body aches, they can have different causes and may require different medical evaluation.

Common signs of dengue may include:
• High fever
• Severe headache
• Pain behind the eyes
• Muscle and joint pain
• Skin rash

Common signs of viral fever may include:
• Fever with cough or sore throat
• Runny or blocked nose
• General body aches
• Fatigue

If your fever lasts more than two days, becomes very high, or is accompanied by persistent vomiting, unusual bleeding, severe weakness, or difficulty breathing, it is important to seek prompt medical attention.

Early assessment and appropriate care can help identify the underlying cause and guide suitable treatment. Staying hydrated, preventing mosquito bites, and maintaining good hygiene are important preventive measures during the monsoon season.

featured_reviews.review_text:
My prev experiences -
* When i was in school i had bald patches suddenly and treatment done here brought my hair back to normal.
* Around 10yrs ago my ear pain was severe and i had hard ear wax when i visited in private hospital they took consultation money and told me to come next day (although i had used ear wax medicine and the wax was soft). I visited KEM next day the treatment was done same day and my ear wax was removed by the doctor in the ENT dept.

Recent visit -
I visited this month dermatology dept. 1st of all the registration queue is huge (7.15-10.30am - 1st opd.. there is afternoon timing as well 12.30-3pm i guess)there are many counters but the crowd is huge as well (1st video), you need aadhaar xerox or pic in phone to register and you get a copy of token no on WhatsApp and sms and 10rs for registration. Doctor will provide the case paper during the visit. They have computers and can access your details.
once you get through the registration you get to the doctor dept. you want to visit and wait in the line ask who's last in line and just sit (there is lots of place/benches). There is staff outside who will guide you and they send you inside sorting as new, old & mbmc staff patients.
It took me approx. 2hrs to meet the doctor. Also for biopsy i was told to purchase nail cutter from outside so my time was wasted there and by the time i was back the concerned doctor was seeing a patient. After collection of sample i was told to go on the 5th floor which i didn't know was the New Bldg(4th pic). It's massive and there too I had to wait a lot just to submit the sample it was around 11am. By the time I leave it was 11.30am (around 4hrs total time).

2nd visit- I went early as usual but the doctor i have to meet was running late that day i also had to collect my report from the new bldg which starts after 9am.  After the long wait around 10.30am i was made to sit outside before the entrance but was told by staff i have to wait more half n hr. Overall by the time everything was done it was 11.30am. (4hrs).

To conclude you need at least half a day to visit and a lot of patience. The staff is good but if public don't listen they have to shout (wouldn't blame the staff for being rude). The washroom was okay but only 1 was available in ladies section near the entrance 1st floor. Medicine are available at the medical on the ground floor and opp the hospital as well. Food options are available on the campus (canteen) and opp the hospital. Walking distance from parel station. Doctors are good and experienced. So especially for such cases i prefer visiting KEM hospital for treatment. I don't have dermatology dept. In the govt hospital in my area so i had to travel here. Else for normal issues i visit nearby govt. Hospitals.

featured_reviews.review_text:
It is with immense pain that I am writing this review after losing my grandmother at KEM Hospital, Parel. Our experience was deeply distressing and disappointing.

Throughout her treatment, we felt that the doctors were not fully transparent with us. We were repeatedly given hope about her recovery, and her condition was often described as stable or improving. However, her sudden deterioration left us shocked and confused. As a family, we now feel that we were not given a clear and honest picture of how critical her situation truly was.

In such sensitive moments, families deserve clarity, honesty, and realistic guidance — even if the truth is difficult. False reassurance or incomplete communication only makes the final loss more traumatic.

The staff nurses appeared inattentive and lacked empathy during crucial times. Communication was poor, and we often had to chase for updates. The management system felt disorganized, adding unnecessary stress to an already painful situation.

Hospitals are not only about treatment; they are about compassion, accountability, and dignity. Sadly, we did not feel that our grandmother received the level of transparency and care she deserved in her final days.

I hope the hospital administration reflects seriously on patient communication, staff behavior, and overall management practices so that other families do not go through what we experienced.

I’m writing this review with a broken heart. My mother-in-law is no longer with us, and I believe DR. SALMAN ALI SAYED (Nephrologist) at this hospital is responsible.
He misdiagnosed her condition - or failed to diagnose it properly at all. Her health deteriorated rapidly under his care. What could have been treated became fatal because of medical negligence.
We trusted this doctor with someone we loved. We believed he would help her. Instead, we lost her.
The rushed appointments, the failure to listen to our concerns, the lack of proper and unnecessary testing - it all added up to a tragedy that didn’t have to happen. This hospital treated her like a SOURCE of REVENUE, not a HUMAN BEING fighting for her life.
She’s gone now. Our family is shattered. And I have to live every day knowing that better care could have saved her.

To anyone reading this:

PLEASE get a second opinion. Ask questions. Demand answers. Don’t trust blindly like we did.

If this review saves even one person from what we went through, then maybe her death won’t be completely meaningless.

We will never get her back. Don’t let this happen to your family.
